Meeting header:

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, really excited to chat through how the quickstart works and what you can get going with the self-serve api.
[00:08] Maya: Hi, thanks, i'm maya. we just want a quick sense of how fast we can get a prototype live and what the differences are between hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:15] Alex: totally. quick overview: redwood offers the hosted api for fastest time to value, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and private/vpc/on-prem for regulated workloads. the PLG quickstart is the hosted path - redeem free credits, sign up, and you can be at first token in under 10 minutes.
[00:30] Samir: hi, i'm samir, i work on performance and infra. if you care about latency we can show p95 numbers for models and we also have options like quantized variants and batching to manage cost.
[00:45] Liam: our main use case is a customer support assistant that uses our internal kbs and call transcripts. data residency is a must for some customers and we also need SOC 2 type controls. curious about encryption and audit logs.
[01:05] Alex: good callout. for the quickstart you'll be on the hosted environment which is SOC 2 compliant, we can share the security pack; for strict residency and dedicated auditor requirements we have the private deployment with customer-managed vpc and kms. dedicated sits in between - reserved gpus but still managed by us.
[01:25] Ravi: what about data retention and egress? we need to ensure PII isn't stored long-term on the hosted side.
[01:33] Jenna: the hosted product has configurable retention policies and enterprise plans include longer log retention/audit options. for PII-sensitive pipelines we recommend either disabling logs or using private deployment with your own kms.
[01:50] Maya: can you walk through the quickstart steps? what is time-to-first-token in practice and what dev work is needed?
[01:57] Alex: absolutely. sign up, claim free credits (we'll send you a redeem code), get an api key. we have a one-click node/snippet in the console: install sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run the sample request - first token in under 60 seconds if you have credentials ready; typical end-to-end from signup to integrated prototype about 10-20 minutes for a simple chat.
[02:20] Samir: sometimes onboarding depends on network egress for customers behind strict proxies, but we can share curl samples and the SDK that handles streaming and reconnects.
[02:35] Liam: are there client libraries? we primarily use python and node.
[02:39] Alex: yes we have official node and python sdks, plus direct rest examples. we'll include the snippets.
[02:46] Maya: cost - high-level, what should we expect for embeddings and chat?
[02:52] Alex: for quickstart we often recommend smaller curated models for testing. embed pipelines are typically cheaper on smaller models; we'll send a starter pricing sheet with example token costs and a sample cost-run for 1k requests/day. also, redwood-optimize suggests batching and caching config which can cut unit cost significantly.
[03:15] Ravi: latency numbers? p95?
[03:18] Samir: on hosted for the medium-size chat model you can expect p95 ~ 180-350ms for short contexts, larger contexts are higher. dedicated gives more predictable throughput and lower variance. for strict low-latency we can recommend pinned instances on dedicated.
[03:36] Liam: we're also evaluating aws bedrock and openai; how do you compare?
[03:42] Alex: great question. openai has a broad model offering but we differentiate on production controls, predictable economics and rollout tooling. bedrock is tightly coupled to aws and might solve infra for you, but if you need multi-region failover and straightforward dev experience the redwood approach often wins for engineering velocity.
[04:05] Maya: what's included in the free credits? are there any gotchas?
[04:09] Alex: credits cover api usage for a limited period and are redeemable via the console link we'll send. they are intended for prototyping - large-scale benchmark runs should be discussed so we can ensure quota and capacity.
[04:22] Maya: how would a pilot look? what are success metrics?
[04:26] Samir: typical pilot: 2 weeks, run on hosted with sample prompts; success metrics: p95 latency under your SLO (you mentioned ~300ms), answer accuracy/utility compared to baseline, and a cost-per-conversation metric. we can instrument traces and token-level cost breakdown.
[04:45] Liam: security - can you outline sso/saml, audit logs, kms integration?
[04:50] Jenna: yes. enterprise plans include SSO via SAML/SCIM, role-based access controls, audit logs, and we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments; hosted keys are encrypted at rest and we provide key-rotation guidance. we'll attach the security pack in the follow-up.
[05:10] Ravi: for the integrations team, are there any platform dependencies e.g. k8s networking or special firewall rules?
[05:18] Samir: if you're using hosted nothing special, just allow outbound TLS to our api endpoints. for private/vpc there are network peering steps and we provide a runbook; we'll include a checklist.
[05:33] Maya: any case studies for customer support automation?
[05:36] Alex: yes, we'll link a couple - short notes in the follow-up deck: how customers reduced avg handle time by 20-30% and lowered escalations with a hybrid retrieval augmentation approach.
[05:52] Liam: about the retrieval stack: do you offer embeddings and a managed vector db or do we need our own?
[05:59] Alex: redwood supports embeddings generation in the api and integrates with common vectorstores; we don't force a managed vector db - you can use your existing infra or plug a managed store. our optimize toolkit gives model/quantization recs for embeddings.
[06:18] Maya: how soon can we start the pilot?
[06:21] Alex: as soon as you redeem the credits - i'll send the link right after this call. assume couple hours to onboard devs, then sample requests.
[06:30] Ravi: any limits on streaming or long-running chat sessions?
[06:34] Samir: streaming is supported, we have token/connection limits to protect stability; for longer sessions we recommend prefix caching and kv cache strategies - we can doc that.
[06:50] Maya: we'd like to run a small benchmark: 1k requests/day for customer support prompts, measure p95 and cost. can you help configure that?
[06:58] Alex: yes we'll provide a benchmark template and starter config. samir will suggest the model and quantization profile.
[07:06] Liam: on dedicated vs hosted: if pilot goes well and we need steady throughput, what's the lead time for dedicated?
[07:12] Jenna: dedicated provisioning is typically 2-6 weeks depending on capacity and region; for urgent production we offer reserved burst options.
[07:22] Maya: any procurement/legal notes for initial contract?
[07:25] Alex: for the quickstart it's self-serve, no contract. for dedicated/private you'll go through sales+legal and we can provide standard t&c; we'll attach a procurement checklist.
[07:38] Ravi: ok. who will own the security review?
[07:41] Maya: i'll coordinate and get our security engineer on the call; ravi will collect logs and requirements.
[07:46] Alex: perfect - next steps we'll send the quickstart link, free credits, pricing sheet and security pack, and schedule the security deep-dive.
[07:54] Maya: sounds good. thanks all.

[End of meeting]
